doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Not an inquisitive child; the dead pet rabbit
summary: He says he was never inquisitive or a tinkerer and recalls screaming when his pet rabbit died.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Why do you think that is?

Because I’m just not. For example, people talk about – different subjects come up, and people say, did you know so-and-so’s wife? or did you know this? No. I didn’t know that, because unless in some way I was in a direct contact with someone about something or with a subject or a reasoning, I didn’t inquire much about anything. I read a lot and tried to learn everything I could about everything from reading, and then finally when I got into school, but not very – kids are inquisitive. They like to find out about what makes this work. I didn’t have any of that going on for me.
So you weren’t taking the wings off of butterflies?
And taking things apart and putting them back together.

I remember the only pet I had was a rabbit, and I didn’t want to touch him. I came back in the backyard one day in New Orleans and the rabbit was dead. I started screaming and crying and going on about it. I remember that. But I didn’t want to touch him. I didn’t like the food they had him on.
